newsitem.title: OMAN: Israel trade office operating despite Oman freeze.
newsitem.headline: Israel trade office operating despite Oman freeze.

text.p: Israel's trade office in the Gulf Arab state of Oman has not been informed of a Omani decision to freeze ties with the Jewish state and was operating normally, its head Oded Ben-Haim said on Tuesday.
"We received nothing official on the freezing of contacts between Oman and Israel and we are operating normally to promote economic relations between the two countries," he said.
"Omani and Israeli companies have done and are doing business though it is still at a small scale," he told Reuters.
He said the trade office has moved to new premises "which is a sign of stabilisation in relations..."
Oman said last week it had frozen ties with the Israeli government because Israel had not honoured its commitments to the Palestinian leadership.

Israel signed a deal with the Palestinian authorities last year to withdraw its troops from major West Bank towns, but delayed a pullout from Hebron after a wave of militant Islamic suicide bombigns in Israel in February and March.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who in May defeated the government that negotiated the deal, put it on hold, saying changes were needed to enhance Jewish settlers' security.
Oman and Qatar have gone further than their Gulf Arab allies to establish ties with Israel, but stopped short of full diplomatic ties pending resolution of all Arab-Israeli conflicts.
